sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: GENERAL PROVISIONS

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: The purpose of this Directive is to contribute to the proper functioning of the internal market and achieve a high level of consumer protection by approximating the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States on unfair commercial practices harming consumers' economic interests.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: For the purposes of this Directive:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘consumer’ means any natural person who, in commercial practices covered by this Directive, is acting for purposes which are outside his trade, business, craft or profession;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘trader’ means any natural or legal person who, in commercial practices covered by this Directive, is acting for purposes relating to his trade, business, craft or profession and anyone acting in the name of or on behalf of a trader;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘product’ means any good or service including immovable property, digital service and digital content, as well as rights and obligations;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘business-to-consumer commercial practices’ (hereinafter also referred to as commercial practices) means any act, omission, course of conduct or representation, commercial communication including advertising and marketing, by a trader, directly connected with the promotion, sale or supply of a product to consumers;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘to materially distort the economic behaviour of consumers’ means using a commercial practice to appreciably impair the consumer's ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing the consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘code of conduct’ means an agreement or set of rules not imposed by law, regulation or administrative provision of a Member State which defines the behaviour of traders who undertake to be bound by the code in relation to one or more particular commercial practices or business sectors;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘code owner’ means any entity, including a trader or group of traders, which is responsible for the formulation and revision of a code of conduct and/or for monitoring compliance with the code by those who have undertaken to be bound by it;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘professional diligence’ means the standard of special skill and care which a trader may reasonably be expected to exercise towards consumers, commensurate with honest market practice and/or the general principle of good faith in the trader's field of activity;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘invitation to purchase’ means a commercial communication which indicates characteristics of the product and the price in a way appropriate to the means of the commercial communication used and thereby enables the consumer to make a purchase;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘undue influence’ means exploiting a position of power in relation to the consumer so as to apply pressure, even without using or threatening to use physical force, in a way which significantly limits the consumer's ability to make an informed decision;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘transactional decision’ means any decision taken by a consumer concerning whether, how and on what terms to purchase, make payment in whole or in part for, retain or dispose of a product or to exercise a contractual right in relation to the product, whether the consumer decides to act or to refrain from acting;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘regulated profession’ means a professional activity or a group of professional activities, access to which or the pursuit of which, or one of the modes of pursuing which, is conditional, directly or indirectly, upon possession of specific professional qualifications, pursuant to laws, regulations or administrative provisions;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘ranking’ means the relative prominence given to products, as presented, organised or communicated by the trader, irrespective of the technological means used for such presentation, organisation or communication;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: ‘online marketplace’ means a service using software, including a website, part of a website or an application, operated by or on behalf of a trader which allows consumers to conclude distance contracts with other traders or consumers.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Internal market

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall neither restrict the freedom to provide services nor restrict the free movement of goods for reasons falling within the field approximated by this Directive.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: UNFAIR COMMERCIAL PRACTICES

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: A commercial practice shall be unfair if:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it is contrary to the requirements of professional diligence,

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it materially distorts or is likely to materially distort the economic behaviour with regard to the product of the average consumer whom it reaches or to whom it is addressed, or of the average member of the group when a commercial practice is directed to a particular group of consumers.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: In particular, commercial practices shall be unfair which:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: are misleading as set out in Articles 6 and 7,

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: are aggressive as set out in Articles 8 and 9.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Misleading commercial practices

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Misleading actions

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: A commercial practice shall be regarded as misleading if it contains false information and is therefore untruthful or in any way, including overall presentation, deceives or is likely to deceive the average consumer, even if the information is factually correct, in relation to one or more of the following elements, and in either case causes or is likely to cause him to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the existence or nature of the product;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the main characteristics of the product, such as its availability, benefits, risks, execution, composition, accessories, after-sale customer assistance and complaint handling, method and date of manufacture or provision, delivery, fitness for purpose, usage, quantity, specification, geographical or commercial origin or the results to be expected from its use, or the results and material features of tests or checks carried out on the product;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the extent of the trader's commitments, the motives for the commercial practice and the nature of the sales process, any statement or symbol in relation to direct or indirect sponsorship or approval of the trader or the product;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the price or the manner in which the price is calculated, or the existence of a specific price advantage;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the need for a service, part, replacement or repair;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the nature, attributes and rights of the trader or his agent, such as his identity and assets, his qualifications, status, approval, affiliation or connection and ownership of industrial, commercial or intellectual property rights or his awards and distinctions;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the consumer's rights, including the right to replacement or reimbursement under Directive 1999/44/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 May 1999 on certain aspects of the sale of consumer goods and associated guarantees ( 1 ), or the risks he may face.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: A commercial practice shall also be regarded as misleading if, in its factual context, taking account of all its features and circumstances, it causes or is likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise, and it involves:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any marketing of a product, including comparative advertising, which creates confusion with any products, trade marks, trade names or other distinguishing marks of a competitor;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: non-compliance by the trader with commitments contained in codes of conduct by which the trader has undertaken to be bound, where:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the commitment is not aspirational but is firm and is capable of being verified,

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the trader indicates in a commercial practice that he is bound by the code;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any marketing of a good, in one Member State, as being identical to a good marketed in other Member States, while that good has significantly different composition or characteristics, unless justified by legitimate and objective factors.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Misleading omissions

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: In the case of an invitation to purchase, the following information shall be regarded as material, if not already apparent from the context:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the main characteristics of the product, to an extent appropriate to the medium and the product;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the geographical address and the identity of the trader, such as his trading name and, where applicable, the geographical address and the identity of the trader on whose behalf he is acting;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the price inclusive of taxes, or where the nature of the product means that the price cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the manner in which the price is calculated, as well as, where appropriate, all additional freight, delivery or postal charges or, where these charges cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the fact that such additional charges may be payable;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the arrangements for payment, delivery and performance, if they depart from the requirements of professional diligence;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: for products and transactions involving a right of withdrawal or cancellation, the existence of such a right;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: for products offered on online marketplaces, whether the third party offering the products is a trader or not, on the basis of the declaration of that third party to the provider of the online marketplace.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Aggressive commercial practices

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: A commercial practice shall be regarded as aggressive if, in its factual context, taking account of all its features and circumstances, by harassment, coercion, including the use of physical force, or undue influence, it significantly impairs or is likely to significantly impair the average consumer's freedom of choice or conduct with regard to the product and thereby causes him or is likely to cause him to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Use of harassment, coercion and undue influence

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: In determining whether a commercial practice uses harassment, coercion, including the use of physical force, or undue influence, account shall be taken of:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: its timing, location, nature or persistence;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the use of threatening or abusive language or behaviour;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the exploitation by the trader of any specific misfortune or circumstance of such gravity as to impair the consumer's judgement, of which the trader is aware, to influence the consumer's decision with regard to the product;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any onerous or disproportionate non-contractual barriers imposed by the trader where a consumer wishes to exercise rights under the contract, including rights to terminate a contract or to switch to another product or another trader;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any threat to take any action that cannot legally be taken.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: CODES OF CONDUCT

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: This Directive does not exclude the control, which Member States may encourage, of unfair commercial practices by code owners and recourse to such bodies by the persons or organisations referred to in Article 11 if proceedings before such bodies are in addition to the court or administrative proceedings referred to in that Article.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Recourse to such control bodies shall never be deemed the equivalent of foregoing a means of judicial or administrative recourse as provided for in Article 11.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: FINAL PROVISIONS

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall ensure that adequate and effective means exist to combat unfair commercial practices in order to enforce compliance with the provisions of this Directive in the interest of consumers.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Such means shall include legal provisions under which persons or organisations regarded under national law as having a legitimate interest in combating unfair commercial practices, including competitors, may:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: take legal action against such unfair commercial practices;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: bring such unfair commercial practices before an administrative authority competent either to decide on complaints or to initiate appropriate legal proceedings.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: It shall be for each Member State to decide which of these facilities shall be available and whether to enable the courts or administrative authorities to require prior recourse to other established means of dealing with complaints, including those referred to in Article 10. These facilities shall be available regardless of whether the consumers affected are in the territory of the Member State where the trader is located or in another Member State.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: It shall be for each Member State to decide:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: whether these legal facilities may be directed separately or jointly against a number of traders from the same economic sector;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: whether these legal facilities may be directed against a code owner where the relevant code promotes non-compliance with legal requirements.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Under the legal provisions referred to in paragraph 1, Member States shall confer upon the courts or administrative authorities powers enabling them, in cases where they deem such measures to be necessary taking into account all the interests involved and in particular the public interest:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: to order the cessation of, or to institute appropriate legal proceedings for an order for the cessation of, unfair commercial practices;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: if the unfair commercial practice has not yet been carried out but is imminent, to order the prohibition of the practice, or to institute appropriate legal proceedings for an order for the prohibition of the practice,

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: even without proof of actual loss or damage or of intention or negligence on the part of the trader.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall also make provision for the measures referred to in the first subparagraph to be taken under an accelerated procedure:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: on the understanding that it is for each Member State to decide which of the two options to select.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Furthermore, Member States may confer upon the courts or administrative authorities powers enabling them, with a view to eliminating the continuing effects of unfair commercial practices the cessation of which has been ordered by a final decision:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: to require publication of that decision in full or in part and in such form as they deem adequate;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: to require in addition the publication of a corrective statement.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: The administrative authorities referred to in paragraph 1 must:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: be composed so as not to cast doubt on their impartiality;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: have adequate powers, where they decide on complaints, to monitor and enforce the observance of their decisions effectively;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: normally give reasons for their decisions.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Where the powers referred to in paragraph 2 are exercised exclusively by an administrative authority, reasons for its decisions shall always be given. Furthermore, in this case, provision must be made for procedures whereby improper or unreasonable exercise of its powers by the administrative authority or improper or unreasonable failure to exercise the said powers can be the subject of judicial review.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Courts and administrative authorities: substantiation of claims

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall confer upon the courts or administrative authorities powers enabling them in the civil or administrative proceedings provided for in Article 11:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: to require the trader to furnish evidence as to the accuracy of factual claims in relation to a commercial practice if, taking into account the legitimate interest of the trader and any other party to the proceedings, such a requirement appears appropriate on the basis of the circumstances of the particular case;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: to consider factual claims as inaccurate if the evidence demanded in accordance with (a) is not furnished or is deemed insufficient by the court or administrative authority.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall ensure that the following non-exhaustive and indicative criteria are taken into account for the imposition of penalties, where appropriate:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the nature, gravity, scale and duration of the infringement;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any action taken by the trader to mitigate or remedy the damage suffered by consumers;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any previous infringements by the trader;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: the financial benefits gained or losses avoided by the trader due to the infringement, if the relevant data are available;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: penalties imposed on the trader for the same infringement in other Member States in cross-border cases where information about such penalties is available through the mechanism established by Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 );

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: any other aggravating or mitigating factors applicable to the circumstances of the case.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall ensure that when penalties are to be imposed in accordance with Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394, they include the possibility either to impose fines through administrative procedures or to initiate legal proceedings for the imposition of fines, or both, the maximum amount of such fines being at least 4 % of the trader’s annual turnover in the Member State or Member States concerned. Without prejudice to that Regulation, Member States may, for national constitutional reasons, restrict the imposition of fines to:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: infringements of Articles 6, 7, 8, 9 and of Annex I to this Directive; and

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: a trader’s continued use of a commercial practice that has been found to be unfair by the competent national authority or court, when that commercial practice is not an infringement referred to in point (a).

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Amendments to Directive 84/450/EEC

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Directive 84/450/EEC is hereby amended as follows:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 1 shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: The purpose of this Directive is to protect traders against misleading advertising and the unfair consequences thereof and to lay down the conditions under which comparative advertising is permitted.’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: in Article 2:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: “trader” means any natural or legal person who is acting for purposes relating to his trade, craft, business or profession and any one acting in the name of or on behalf of a trader.’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: “code owner” means any entity, including a trader or group of traders, which is responsible for the formulation and revision of a code of conduct and/or for monitoring compliance with the code by those who have undertaken to be bound by it.’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 3a shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Comparative advertising shall, as far as the comparison is concerned, be permitted when the following conditions are met:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it is not misleading within the meaning of Articles 2(2), 3 and 7(1) of this Directive or Articles 6 and 7 of Directive 2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2005 concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market ( *1 );

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it compares goods or services meeting the same needs or intended for the same purpose;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it objectively compares one or more material, relevant, verifiable and representative features of those goods and services, which may include price;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it does not discredit or denigrate the trade marks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods, services, activities, or circumstances of a competitor;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: for products with designation of origin, it relates in each case to products with the same designation;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it does not take unfair advantage of the reputation of a trade mark, trade name or other distinguishing marks of a competitor or of the designation of origin of competing products;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it does not present goods or services as imitations or replicas of goods or services bearing a protected trade mark or trade name;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: it does not create confusion among traders, between the advertiser and a competitor or between the advertiser's trade marks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods or services and those of a competitor.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 4(1) shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall ensure that adequate and effective means exist to combat misleading advertising in order to enforce compliance with the provisions on comparative advertising in the interest of traders and competitors. Such means shall include legal provisions under which persons or organisations regarded under national law as having a legitimate interest in combating misleading advertising or regulating comparative advertising may:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: take legal action against such advertising;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: bring such advertising before an administrative authority competent either to decide on complaints or to initiate appropriate legal proceedings.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: It shall be for each Member State to decide which of these facilities shall be available and whether to enable the courts or administrative authorities to require prior recourse to other established means of dealing with complaints, including those referred to in Article 5.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: whether these legal facilities may be directed against a code owner where the relevant code promotes non-compliance with legal requirements.’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 7(1) shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: This Directive shall not preclude Member States from retaining or adopting provisions with a view to ensuring more extensive protection, with regard to misleading advertising, for traders and competitors.’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Amendments to Directives 97/7/EC and 2002/65/EC

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 9 of Directive 97/7/EC shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Inertia selling

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Given the prohibition of inertia selling practices laid down in Directive 2005/29/EC of 11 May 2005of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market ( *2 ), Member States shall take the measures necessary to exempt the consumer from the provision of any consideration in cases of unsolicited supply, the absence of a response not constituting consent.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Article 9 of Directive 2002/65/EC shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Given the prohibition of inertia selling practices laid down in Directive 2005/29/EC of 11 May 2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market ( *3 ) and without prejudice to the provisions of Member States' legislation on the tacit renewal of distance contracts, when such rules permit tacit renewal, Member States shall take measures to exempt the consumer from any obligation in the event of unsolicited supplies, the absence of a reply not constituting consent.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Amendments to Directive 98/27/EC and Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: In the Annex to Directive 98/27/EC, point 1 shall be replaced by the following:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Directive 2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2005 concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market (OJ L 149, 11.6.2005, p. 22).’

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: In the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 October 2004 on cooperation between national authorities responsible for the enforcement of the consumer protection law (the Regulation on consumer protection cooperation) ( 4 ) the following point shall be added:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall take appropriate measures to inform consumers of the national law transposing this Directive and shall, where appropriate, encourage traders and code owners to inform consumers of their codes of conduct.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Transposition

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Member States shall adopt and publish the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 12 June 2007. They shall forthwith inform the Commission thereof and inform the Commission of any subsequent amendments without delay.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: They shall apply those measures by 12 December 2007. When Member States adopt those measures, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or be accompanied by such a reference on the occasion of their official publication. Member States shall determine how such reference is to be made.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Entry into force

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: This Directive shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: This Directive is addressed to the Member States.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: COMMERCIAL PRACTICES WHICH ARE IN ALL CIRCUMSTANCES CONSIDERED UNFAIR

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming to be a signatory to a code of conduct when the trader is not.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Displaying a trust mark, quality mark or equivalent without having obtained the necessary authorisation.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming that a code of conduct has an endorsement from a public or other body which it does not have.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming that a trader (including his commercial practices) or a product has been approved, endorsed or authorised by a public or private body when he/it has not or making such a claim without complying with the terms of the approval, endorsement or authorisation.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Making an invitation to purchase products at a specified price without disclosing the existence of any reasonable grounds the trader may have for believing that he will not be able to offer for supply or to procure another trader to supply, those products or equivalent products at that price for a period that is, and in quantities that are, reasonable having regard to the product, the scale of advertising of the product and the price offered (bait advertising).

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Making an invitation to purchase products at a specified price and then:

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: refusing to show the advertised item to consumers;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: refusing to take orders for it or deliver it within a reasonable time;

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: demonstrating a defective sample of it,

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: with the intention of promoting a different product (bait and switch)

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Falsely stating that a product will only be available for a very limited time, or that it will only be available on particular terms for a very limited time, in order to elicit an immediate decision and deprive consumers of sufficient opportunity or time to make an informed choice.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Undertaking to provide after-sales service to consumers with whom the trader has communicated prior to a transaction in a language which is not an official language of the Member State where the trader is located and then making such service available only in another language without clearly disclosing this to the consumer before the consumer is committed to the transaction.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Stating or otherwise creating the impression that a product can legally be sold when it cannot.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Presenting rights given to consumers in law as a distinctive feature of the trader's offer.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Using editorial content in the media to promote a product where a trader has paid for the promotion without making that clear in the content or by images or sounds clearly identifiable by the consumer (advertorial). This is without prejudice to Council Directive 89/552/EEC ( 5 ).

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Providing search results in response to a consumer’s online search query without clearly disclosing any paid advertisement or payment specifically for achieving higher ranking of products within the search results.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Making a materially inaccurate claim concerning the nature and extent of the risk to the personal security of the consumer or his family if the consumer does not purchase the product.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Promoting a product similar to a product made by a particular manufacturer in such a manner as deliberately to mislead the consumer into believing that the product is made by that same manufacturer when it is not.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Establishing, operating or promoting a pyramid promotional scheme where a consumer gives consideration for the opportunity to receive compensation that is derived primarily from the introduction of other consumers into the scheme rather than from the sale or consumption of products.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming that the trader is about to cease trading or move premises when he is not.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming that products are able to facilitate winning in games of chance.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Falsely claiming that a product is able to cure illnesses, dysfunction or malformations.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Passing on materially inaccurate information on market conditions or on the possibility of finding the product with the intention of inducing the consumer to acquire the product at conditions less favourable than normal market conditions.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Claiming in a commercial practice to offer a competition or prize promotion without awarding the prizes described or a reasonable equivalent.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Describing a product as ‘gratis’, ‘free’, ‘without charge’ or similar if the consumer has to pay anything other than the unavoidable cost of responding to the commercial practice and collecting or paying for delivery of the item.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Including in marketing material an invoice or similar document seeking payment which gives the consumer the impression that he has already ordered the marketed product when he has not.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Falsely claiming or creating the impression that the trader is not acting for purposes relating to his trade, business, craft or profession, or falsely representing oneself as a consumer.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Creating the false impression that after-sales service in relation to a product is available in a Member State other than the one in which the product is sold.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Reselling events tickets to consumers if the trader acquired them by using automated means to circumvent any limit imposed on the number of tickets that a person can buy or any other rules applicable to the purchase of tickets.

sections.heading: Official source update
sections.text: Stating that reviews of a product are submitted by consumers who have actually used or purchased the product without taking reasonable and proportionate steps to check that they originate from such consumers.
